full_judgment: 5. Now with regard to the bonafide requirement, it appears that the learned S.C.C. Judge has rejected the prayer on the ground that the plaintiff had other houses and further that there was vacant space adjoining the suit premises where construction can be made Section 18(1) (e) lays down that where the premises are bonafide required by the landlord either for purposes of building or re-building or for his own occupation or for the occupation of any person for whose benefit the premises are held or where the landlord can show any cause which may be deemed satisfactory by the court, the prayer should not be refused. The learned S.C.C. Judge appear to have lost sight of the fact that it was the petitioner’s positive case that he wanted to construct a building on the suit land and an approved plan was also filed which was marked as exhibit '4' in the case. According to law, bonafide requirement also included building or re-building but unfortunately the court below rejected the prayer on the presumption that since the plaintiff had other houses, there was no bonafide requirement. The learned Judge did not at all consider the petitioner's case and exhibit '4' filed by the plaintiff in support of his Case. I am, therefore, satisfied that the plaintiff has made out a case of bonafide requirement which is substantiated by the evidence on record. Having regard to these facts and circumstances and my discussion above, the findings of the learned S.C.C. Judge cannot be sustained.
